A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison, including material moved between pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original TSP experiments comparing reinforcement learning, supervised fine-tuning and local search, together with scaling fits and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds leave-one-out analysis of the fitted scaling laws.

M1.justification: The Transformer/Pointer Network architecture, PPO with compositional value estimates, supervised objective and local-search procedures remain unchanged. The new resampling analysis does not modify the models or training algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Euclidean TSP coverage, including node scaling from 5 to 50 and spatial dimensions up to 100. VRP, OP, RSP and NLP tasks are newly discussed as possible future applications, not evaluated.

E2.justification: The RL/SFT comparisons, 2-opt and 2-exchange analyses, and Figure 17 comparison of greedy-rollout, state-value and compositional-value baselines are retained. Newly cited routing methods are not added to the experiments.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model scales, evaluation datasets, sample sizes and suboptimality metrics remain unchanged. The added leave-one-out calculations assess uncertainty in existing fits without changing the underlying evaluation design.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds sensitivity analysis that omits individual training runs and compares node-scaling fits with fixed versus refitted offset gamma. This tests dependence on individual scales; the earlier convergence, loss, landscape and baseline analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 acknowledges single-seed fit imprecision without quantifying uncertainty in the central fitted exponents. v2 adds systematic leave-one-out means, standard deviations, skewness and extrema across parameter, compute, optimal-model-size, node and dimension scaling fits in Table 4. These quantify fit sensitivity, not additional training seeds or across-seed uncertainty.

E6.justification: The existing full-data fits and experimental outcomes are retained. New Table 4 reports sensitivity results, including RL node-exponent ranges of 1.83–1.95 with fixed gamma and 1.81–2.22 with refitted gamma. These are additional analysis results, not performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 2.5 adds the explicit validity condition n >= 3 to the (n−1)!/2 tour-count formula and clarifies its symmetry factors. This is a limited mathematical qualification; Appendix I retains the existing lemmas, theorems and derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: neural and problem-complexity scaling laws for TSP, their extrapolation limits, the local-search analogy and the 128-million-solution dataset. The new analysis supports these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 7 makes single-problem coverage the principal limitation and explicitly requires broader validation before treating complexity scaling as a general principle. It expands applicability and practical-use discussion. Appendix A also interprets fit sensitivity and distinguishes leave-one-out variation from multi-seed variation.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly states that individual leave-one-out fits are available in the existing project repository. Hardware, architecture documentation, training hyperparameters and other code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references covering sparse-model scaling, other routing problems, neural routing methods and PyTorch, and expands discussion of data pruning. The central positioning relative to prior scaling-law and combinatorial-optimization research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and mathematical-explanation edits, separates neural scaling-law theory within related work, and expands the discussion with real-world-domain and practical-implication paragraphs. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the leave-one-out statistics table and reformats Figure 3 with taller panels and an inset legend. Existing figures and tables are redistributed through page reflow, including separation of Figures 9 and 10; their retained results are not new experiments.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity statistics make the central scaling fits more assessable, while the revised discussion more clearly limits extrapolation and generalization. These are useful improvements, but the main scaling experiments still use one seed per scale and remain confined to TSP. The revision improves evidential transparency without resolving those broader limitations.
